findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body: After callers invoke the disposer, later `"message"` events still invoke `handler` because the callback is empty. This breaks the established teardown contract and causes stale callbacks and listener accumulation across repeated attach/dispose cycles.

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
Calling the disposer after `attach()` no longer unregisters the handler. Any subsequent `"message"` invokes a supposedly cancelled handler, causing post-teardown state updates and retaining handler references across repeated attach/dispose cycles.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
After callers invoke the cleanup function, any subsequent `"message"` event still invokes `handler`. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate stale listeners, breaking the established teardown contract and potentially causing duplicate processing or listener leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
On a long-lived socket, repeated `attach()`/cleanup cycles now retain every handler indefinitely. This causes unbounded memory growth, duplicate message processing, and callbacks after owners are disposed.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
